newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai rice prices steady this week in quiet market.
newsitem.headline: Thai rice prices steady this week in quiet market.

text.p: Thai rice prices were mostly steady this week in subdued trade as buyers awaited the arrival of new crop supplies in the market later this month, trade sources said on Thursday.
There were no substantial buying orders. Brunei bought 33,000 tonnes of high quality rice on a government-to-government basis for 1997 delivery.
"There are no new leads in the market. The Brunei purchase barely raised anyone's pulse. Overall, the actual demand remained weak and our prices are not very attractive," said one rice exporter.
"But the prices are expected to be lower once more rice from the new harvest enters the market later this month," he said.
Thai 100 percent B benchmark rice was quoted around $330-355 per tonne FOB Bangkok. Thai 100 percent fragrant rice was quoted at $610-615 on the same basis.
Although buying from foreigners was slow, the prices were steady because millers also slowed down milling due to rains and lower milling margins.
"Demand is slow and exporters only bought hand to mouth. There is no incentive to mill large quantities of rice as paddy prices were steady but milled rice prices slid," said one rice miller.

The Commerce Ministry recently launched measures to support domestic rice prices as fresh output is coming to the market. It will buy up to one million tonnes of rice to meet its government-to-government export obligations.
At Thai ports, ships were loading around 45,100 tonnes of rice for shipment to China, Guam, Iran, Malaysia, Nigeria and Singapore.
Thailand exported about 4.39 million tonnes of rice between January 1-November 5 compared with 4.96 million tonnes during the same period in 1995.
